--- title: "Visualizing Water: Sankey Diagrams (draft)" description: | Part 2: custom data-driven flow charts using Highcharts.js and networkD3 (IWMI). date: 2021-10-01 status: DRAFT (do not cite) citation: false funding: IWMI draft: true freeze: true categories: - imwi - hydrology --- This notebook is Part 2 of a code playground for hydrologic model visualization. In [Part 1](../2021-10-16-svg/) we focused on `D3.js`, here we test network and hierarchical visuals using higher-level graphic libraries [Highchart.js](https://www.highcharts.com/) and [networkD3](http://christophergandrud.github.io/networkD3/). The 2 libraries are built on top of D3 but they come with sample configurations and R and Python clients, making it easier to build dynamic charts, esp. Sankey, treemaps, network and flow diagrams with significantly less code. The approach here is inspired by: 1. TruthStudio for the Nature Conservancy's [static illustrations](https://truthstudio.com/portfolio_page/visualizing-water/) of the Colorado River basin's withdrawals and consumption. 2. [Curmi et al. 2013](https://researchgate.net/publication/257673216_Visualising_a_Stochastic_Model_of_Californian_Water_Resources_Using_Sankey_Diagrams) 3. Lancaster University [Food-Energy Flows](https://github.com/csaladenes/food-energy-flows) diagram ::: {.cell .column-page-right layout-ncol="2"} ```{.r .cell-code} c( "./_fig/sankey_truthstudio_1.gif", "./_fig/sankey_truthstudio_2.gif", "./_fig/sankey_curmi_2013.png", "./_fig/sankey_lancaster.png" ) |> include_graphics() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./_fig/sankey_truthstudio_1.gif) ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./_fig/sankey_truthstudio_2.gif) ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./_fig/sankey_curmi_2013.png){width=680} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./_fig/sankey_lancaster.png){width=1024} ::: ::: ::: {.cell .column-page-right} ```{.r .cell-code} # Load yearly dataset generated in Part 1 data <- fread(here("../2021-10-16-svg/data/data.csv")) knitr::kable(data[1:10, ]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |CLASS |SUBCLASS |VARIABLE | VALUE|iso3 |sheet | year| |:------|:-------------|:-----------------------|--------:|:----|:------|----:| |INFLOW |PRECIPITATION |Rainfall | 12.44304|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |PRECIPITATION |Snowfall | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |PRECIPITATION |Precipitation recycling | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |SURFACE WATER |Main riverstem | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |SURFACE WATER |Tributaries | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |SURFACE WATER |Utilized surface water | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |SURFACE WATER |Flood | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |GROUNDWATER |Natural | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |GROUNDWATER |Utilized | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| |INFLOW |OTHER |Desalinized | 0.00000|ken |sheet1 | 2003| ::: ::: # Sankey Diagram {#sankey} A Sankey diagra is a type of directed network graph in which the width of the arrows (vertices) is proportional to the flow rate. Here we use R library [`networkD3`](http://christophergandrud.github.io/networkD3/) to build the charts (chart configurations built in R can be exported to vanilla Javascript). First we define a default theme for Highcharts, which we'll reuse across visuals. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hc_theme_iwmi <- function( hc, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL, label = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL, exporting = TRUE, credits = FALSE, ... ) { thm <- hc_theme( chart = list( backgroundColor = "transparent" ), # Don't use semantic colors colors = unname(pal), title = list( style = list(color = "#333", fontSize = "16px"), align = "left" ), subtitle = list( style = list(color = '#777', fontSize = "13px"), align = "left" ), legend = list( enabled = TRUE, itemStyle = list(color = "#777"), verticalAlign = "top", align = "left", itemHoverStyle = list(color = "#333") ), xAxis = list( title = list(enabled = FALSE), dateTimeLabelFormats = list( day = '%e %b', week = '%e %b %y', month = '%b-%y', year = '%Y' ) ), yAxis = list( title = list(enabled = FALSE) ), tooltip = list( enabled = TRUE, shared = TRUE, split = FALSE, pointFormat = "{series.name}: {point.y:,.1f}
", xDateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d", dateTimeLabelFormats = "%Y-%m-%d", valueDecimals = 2 ), plotOptions = list( series = list( opacity = .8, connectNulls = TRUE, marker = list(enabled = NA, radius = 3, enabledThreshold = 8), dataLabels = list(enabled = NA, style = list(fontSize = "11px")) ), heatmap = list( marker = list(enabled = TRUE, lineWidth = 6, lineColor = "#fff"), dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, pointFormat = "{point.value:,.0f}") ) ), exporting = list( enabled = exporting, csv = list(dateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d"), buttons = list( contextButton = list( symbolSize = 12, symbolFill = "#fff", symbolStroke = "#777", symbolStrokeWidth = 1.3, menuItems = c( "printChart", "downloadPNG", "downloadSVG", "downloadCSV" ) ) ) ), credits = list( enabled = credits, position = list(align = "left"), href = "https://iwni.cgiar.org/", style = list(fontSize = "11px") ), ... ) p <- hc_add_theme(hc, thm) %>% hc_title(text = title) %>% hc_subtitle(text = subtitle) if (length(label) > 0) { p <- p %>% hc_annotations(list( labels = list( list( text = label, useHTML = TRUE, shape = "rect", point = list(x = x, y = y) ) ) )) } return(p) } ``` ::: Then we reshape our sample Kenya dataset for 2017 into a list of vertices between 2 nodes (with fields `from`, `to`, `value` at minimum). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Draft ``` ::: # Steamgraphs
